question.problem:
Solve for $x$ in $Ax=b$ given that the matrix $A$ is orthogonal, and 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} \\ 0 \\ -2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
The inverse of an orthogonal matrix is equal to its transpose.

Hence, since $A$ is orthogonal, we have ${A}^{-1}={A}^{T}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ {A}^{-1}Ax & ={A}^{-1}b \\ x & ={A}^{-1}b \\ x & ={A}^{T}b \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} \\ 0 \\ -2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
